pages.text: New megaraptor discovered—with its final meal still in its mouth | National Geographic SCIENCE New megaraptor discovered—with its final meal still in its mouth A croc bone locked between the 70-million-year-old predator’s jaws gives scientists a rare look into its life and possibly its last feast. A reconstruction of the newly discovered megaraptor Joaquinraptor casali from Argentina with a Cretaceous-era crocodile arm in its mouth. Illustration by Andrew McAfee, Carnegie Museum of Natural History By Riley Black Published September 23, 2025 While the great Tyrannosaurus rex stalked prehistoric North America, a very different apex predator prowled ancient Argentina: the newly discovered megaraptor Joaquinraptor casali. When paleontologists excavated the dinosaur, they made a tantalizing find. Clenched within its massive jaws was a Cretaceous crocodile’s arm bone. The discovery offers a glimpse into what may have been the carnivore’s last meal some 70 million years ago. “Fossilized behavior, if that’s really what this is, comes along so rarely that you’ve just got to celebrate it when it does,” says Matthew Lamanna , a paleontologist from the Carnegie Museum of Natural History in Pittsburgh, and a National Geographic Explorer . pages.description: A genome from a female found in Croatia shows how conditions from schizophrenia to arthritis are influenced by our ancient human cousins.
pages.text: New Neanderthal Genome Shows How Ancient DNA Affects Your Health | National Geographic This reconstruction of a Neanderthal female unveiled in 2008 was the first made using ancient DNA evidence. Photograph by Joe McNally, Nat Geo Image Collection New Clues to How Neanderthal Genes Affect Your Health A genome from a female found in Croatia shows how conditions from schizophrenia to arthritis are influenced by our ancient human cousins. By Michelle Z. Donahue Published October 5, 2017 • 6 min read If your arthritis is bad today or you’re slathering on aloe for an early autumn sunburn, Neanderthals may be partly to blame. Scientists announced today the second complete, high-quality sequencing of a Neanderthal genome , made using the 52,000-year-old bones of a female found in the Vindija cave in Croatia. 4:05 Together with the genomes from another Neanderthal woman and a host of modern humans, a suite of analyses is yielding new clues about how DNA from Neanderthals contributed to our genetic makeup and might still be affecting us today. For instance, one new study appearing in the journal Science suggests that Neanderthal genes contribute 1.8 to 2.6 percent of the total genetic makeup for people of Eurasian ancestry. That’s slightly up from a previous estimate of 1.5 to 2.1 percent. (Find out about the first solid DNA evidence that Neanderthals and modern humans interbred .) The cruise ship, American Heritage, was left lying on its side in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel Atlantic Asphalt. The collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for. Officials hailed it as a "miracle on the Mississippi". The exact cause of the crash remains under investigation, but US Coast Guard Capt Melanie Burnham said: "There seems to be some type of a loss of steering." New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference on Friday that all credit in the rescue effort should go to first responders who "literally jumped right in to help". "We have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," Moreno said. Calls about the collision began around 13:30 EST (18:30 GMT) on Friday, when people began trying to help passengers escape the boat as it took on water, Port of New Orleans chief Melanie Montroll told the news conference. pages.text: New research challenges the idea that the Maya civilization collapsed | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE Why the idea that the Maya civilization ‘collapsed’ is wrong Laser scans and other evidence show the Maya persisted in rural areas long after big cities collapsed. The Maya are known for their impressive pyramid complexes, like this one known as El Castillo at Chichén Itzá. But local towns and villages sustained these urban areas, and new population estimates of those areas are bringing up questions about whether the Maya really collapsed. Photograph by Paul Nicklen, Nat Geo Image Collection By Joshua Rapp Learn Published December 26, 2024 The Maya created great kingdoms that ruled over tens of thousands of people for centuries in Mesoamerica. But as elaborate capitals like Chichén Itzá and Mayapan and the elites that controlled them rose and fell, the surrounding population that lived in the rural areas around them didn’t change for centuries. The textbook timeline of the Maya civilization goes like this: The culture reached its height , known as the Classic period, between A.D. 200 and 900. Over the next century, urban centers fell apart. By some accounts, the Maya vanished, and scientists have implicated climate, overpopulation, and political unrest in their mysterious demise. While the Maya bounced back during the Postclassic period from A.D. 900 until the arrival of Spanish colonizers around 1540, it supposedly never reached its previous strength. Grand Theft Auto fans have waited 13 long years for the latest edition of the game to be released - and going to extreme lengths to be ready for its launch. GTA 6 will be released at midnight on Thursday - and Victoria Evans, from West Sussex, is not leaving anything to chance. She has her alarm set for 05:00 GMT, and has a day off booked. She says she put the game's release on her leave request form which was approved, she told BBC News, despite the fact her boss "doesn't know what GTA 6 is". She's far from the only one. For the game's launch day, HR software company BrightHR looked at absence data from more than 1.2 million employees from 70,000 businesses across the UK. It found GTA was mentioned in 4.6% of time-off requests by employees. Throughout November and December, it said an estimated 83,000 days had been booked off for the game. And booking leave is only one of the ways fans are making sure for the big day. Others are buying a new console to play it on or even pretending they're halfway around the world to get early access. pages.text: Newfound Fossil Octopus and Squid Were Giants | National Geographic Photo by fir0002, GFDL 1.2. A giant squid in a block of ice at Australia's Melbourne Aquarium. SCIENCE LAELAPS Newfound Fossil Octopus and Squid Were Giants By Riley Black Published March 10, 2015 • 4 min read A good fossil squid is hard to find. The invertebrates are too squishy to leave much behind, and only in truly exceptional circumstances do paleontologists get to see much more than the chitinous supports the cephalopods kept on the inside. Octopus are even more confounding. Without any remnants of an internal shell, the eight-armed quick-change artists are like prehistoric ghosts. But do not despair. The jaws of ancient coleoids give us reason for hope, and have just revealed a pair of prehistoric cephalopods that may have rivaled today’s ocean giants in size. Described by Kazushige Tanabe and colleagues in Acta Palaeontologica Polonica , the two lower jaws were found in roughly 80 million year old rock around Hokkaido, Japan’s Haboro-futamata Dam. Both were preserved in three-dimensional detail, providing Tanabe and coworkers with enough anatomical clues to figure out that they were left behind by previously-unknown species. Octopus and squid beaks can be very informative fossils. That’s because marine biologists have spent a great deal of time studying the chitinous beaks of modern cephalopods. (Not much more than beaks and hooks are left in the guts of squid-eating whales, for example.) Close nicofr77's Diary À portée de train : une carte des boucles vélo accessibles en train, depuis 60 villes Posted by nicofr77 on 2 October 2026 in French (Français) . Last updated on 4 October 2026. Je publie sur Tisseur de Voies, le site où je calcule des boucles vélo avec retour en train, une carte qui répond à une question simple : depuis ma ville, jusqu’où puis-je partir à vélo en prenant un seul train ? On choisit une ville parmi 60 et une durée de train aller, de 0 à 4 heures. La carte montre en rose les véloroutes des boucles qu’on peut rejoindre, et en bleu les gares atteintes, plus foncées quand elles sont proches. Ici, Paris avec une heure de train : 1 763 boucles, contre 323 qui partent des gares parisiennes. Une boucle, c’est un itinéraire à vélo d’une gare à une autre sur des véloroutes balisées, avec un train pour rentrer. Elle compte dès qu’un train aller atteint l’une de ses gares dans la durée choisie. Un classement des 60 villes accompagne la carte : Paris, Strasbourg et Lille en tête, Brest et Quimper en queue. Les véloroutes viennent d’OpenStreetMap et du référentiel national des véloroutes, le fond de carte d’OpenStreetMap. Les durées sortent des horaires publiés en open data par la SNCF, Île-de-France Mobilités, la Région Sud et les Chemins de fer de la Corse : pour chaque trajet, la durée médiane de la ligne la plus rapide qui circule au moins une fois par jour. Seuls les trains sans changement comptent.

Nicole Sanchez Nicole Sanchez serves as Chief of Staff to the Chief Information Officer (CIO). She is also the Department of Energy (DOE) Chief Privacy Officer. She has 20+ years of federal experience, including 16 years specializing in privacy and information governance. Nicole serves as a principal advisor to the CIO, overseeing daily operations of the CIO Office and ensuring alignment of efforts across enterprise IT operations, cybersecurity, privacy, and records management. Nicole excels at advising senior leadership on complex issues with national and international implications, managing privacy programs, and fostering collaboration among a wide variety of stakeholders to solve critical challenges facing federal agencies. Prior to DOE, Nicole held various leadership positions at the Department of Homeland Security, including Deputy Privacy Officer at the Science and Technology Directorate. She advised on privacy implications and mitigations for Artificial Intelligence applications and complex information sharing activities with the Intelligence Community and international partners. Nicole holds a Master of Arts in U.S. Foreign Policy from American University and a Bachelor of Arts in International Relations from the University of Memphis

They are accused of stealing luxury vehicles and shipping them to West Africa. Police in the Peel region of Ontario said they had recovered 96 high-value vehicles concealed in shipping containers. The vehicles, valued at $4.5m (£3.4m) were destined for export via Canadian ports. The trafficking of vehicles from North America and Europe to African countries has been a long-standing concern for law enforcement agencies. The suspects face 231 charges, with arrest warrants issued for others. Police say some of the accused may face deportation after their criminal proceedings are concluded. The arrests followed months of what police described as an "extensive auto theft investigation". The investigations began in March in partnership with Canada's border agency after police identified a warehouse allegedly being used to store stolen vehicles. pages.text: Nike faces religious ban in Libya because it was named after Greek goddess Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Libya's top religious authority rules against wearing Nike clothes 3 November 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Basma El Atti AFP via Getty Images Nike clothes are popular in Libya, although many are counterfeit Libya's highest religious authority, the Dar al-Ifta, has issued a ruling banning Muslims from buying, selling or wearing clothing bearing the Nike logo. The ruling, issued by the Tripoli-based institution, states that the US sportswear giant was named after the Greek goddess of victory and that its famous swoosh logo was inspired by her wings. It argued that wearing clothing displaying the logo amounted to promoting symbols associated "with polytheism," or the worship of more than one god. Libya is home to the ancient Greek city of Cyrene, where archaeological remains include a statue of the Greek goddess of the same name. The religious committee also accused Nike of supporting Israel and called for a boycott of companies that back the country. It referred to a statement issued by its Council for Research and Sharia Studies on 5 November 2023, urging Muslims to boycott Western companies it considers supportive of Israel during the war in Gaza. Her reports air regularly on NPR's critically acclaimed newsmagazines All Things Considered , Morning Edition , and Weekend Edition . Totenberg's coverage of the Supreme Court and legal affairs has won her widespread recognition. She is often featured in documentaries — most recently RBG — that deal with issues before the court. As Newsweek put it, "The mainstays [of NPR] are Morning Edition and All Things Considered . But the creme de la creme is Nina Totenberg." In 1991, her ground-breaking report about University of Oklahoma Law Professor Anita Hill's allegations of sexual harassment by Judge Clarence Thomas led the Senate Judiciary Committee to re-open Thomas's Supreme Court confirmation hearings to consider Hill's charges. NPR received the prestigious George Foster Peabody Award for its gavel-to-gavel coverage — anchored by Totenberg — of both the original hearings and the inquiry into Anita Hill's allegations, and for Totenberg's reports and exclusive interview with Hill. By establishing objective benchmarks traceable to the International System of Units (SI), NIST reduces technical and financial risks, empowering U.S. manufacturers to substitute, recover, and utilize critical materials with precision and confidence.
